While he offered incense in the Temple, the angel Gabriel announced that his barren wife Elizabeth would bear a son to be named John; because he doubted, he was struck mute. When he wrote 'His name is John', his speech returned and he prophesied the Benedictus.
catholic: Zechariah's canticle, the Benedictus (Lk 1:68-79), is prayed every day at Morning Prayer in the Liturgy of the Hours, blessing God for the dawn of salvation and for John's mission as prophet of the Most High. His muteness and restored speech are often contrasted with Mary's faith-filled question at the Annunciation. He and Elizabeth are commemorated together as saints.
know: Priest of the division of Abijah (Lk 1:5).
Struck mute for doubting Gabriel (Lk 1:20).
Wrote 'His name is John' (Lk 1:63).
Spoke the Benedictus (Lk 1:68-79).
feast: September 23 (Sts Zechariah and Elizabeth, Roman Martyrology)

name: Zelophehad
summary: Son of Hepher of the tribe of Manasseh, who died in the wilderness without sons. His five daughters asked for his inheritance, leading to the law that daughters inherit when there is no son.
know: Died in the wilderness, not in Korah's rebellion (Num 27:3).
Had five daughters and no sons.
His case set Israel's inheritance law (Num 27:8-11).

name: Ahitub
summary: Ahitub son of Amariah, of the line of Eleazar son of Aaron, was the father of Zadok the priest.
know: Zadok's descent from Eleazar is traced through him

name: Amos
summary: Amos, a herdsman and dresser of sycamore figs from Tekoa in Judah, was sent to prophesy in the northern kingdom under Jeroboam II (8th century BC). He denounced oppression of the poor, corrupt worship and complacent luxury, saw visions of locusts, fire, a plumb line and summer fruit, and was expelled from Bethel by the priest Amaziah. The book ends with the promise to raise up David's fallen tent.
catholic: Amos is the great prophetic voice of social justice: 'let justice roll on like rivers' (Amos 5:24) informs the Church's social teaching on worship that is inseparable from care for the poor. At the Council of Jerusalem St James quoted Amos 9:11-12 to show that the Gentiles' entry into the Church fulfils God's plan to rebuild David's tent (Acts 15:16-17). Tobit recalls Amos' prophecy that feasts would be turned to mourning (Tob 2:6).
know: 'I was no prophet, nor a prophet's son, but a herdsman' (Amos 7:14).
Expelled from Bethel by Amaziah the priest.
Five visions: locusts, fire, plumb line, summer fruit, the Lord by the altar.
Promise of David's restored tent quoted in Acts 15.

name: Anak
summary: Ancestor of the Anakim, the giant clan of Hebron whose size terrified the ten spies.
know: Son of Arba (Jos 15:13).
The spies felt 'like grasshoppers' beside his descendants (Num 13:33).
Father of Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai.

name: Anna (wife of Tobit)
summary: Tobit's wife, of his own kindred, who supported the household by weaving when he was blind. Her sharp reply when Tobit doubted her honesty, and her daily vigil watching the road for her son, make her one of the most human figures in the book.
catholic: Anna's anxious love for Tobias and her joy at his return (Tob 11:9) show the Old Testament's tender portrait of motherhood; Tobit charges his son to honor her all her days (Tob 4:3-4).
know: Worked as a weaver to support the family (Tob 2:11-12).
Watched the road daily for Tobias (Tob 10:7).
Buried with Tobit by their son (Tob 14:12).

name: Azariah son of Hilkiah
summary: Azariah son of Hilkiah is listed in the high-priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6.
know: Part of the Aaronic line from Eleazar to the Exile

name: Bezalel
summary: Son of Uri, of the tribe of Judah, whom God called by name and filled with the Spirit of God in wisdom and skill. He led the work of making the tabernacle, the ark of the covenant, the mercy seat, the lampstand and the priestly vessels.
catholic: Bezalel is the first person in Scripture said to be 'filled with the Spirit of God' (Exo 31:3), and his gift is artistic: the Church sees in him a patron-figure for sacred art and architecture placed at the service of worship. The ark he made, overshadowed by the cherubim, is in Catholic tradition a type of Mary, the Ark of the New Covenant.
know: Called by name and filled with God's Spirit (Exo 31:1-5).
Made the ark of the covenant (Exo 37:1-9).
Worked with Oholiab and other skilled workers.
His bronze altar still stood at Gibeon in Solomon's day (2 Chr 1:5).

name: Caleb (Chelubai)
summary: Caleb (Chelubai) son of Hezron, brother of Jerahmeel and Ram, heads a large clan list of Judah; Jewish and Christian interpreters traditionally distinguish him from Caleb son of Jephunneh (1 Chr 2:9, 18-24, 42-50).

name: Dan
summary: Jacob's son by Rachel's servant Bilhah; Rachel named him saying 'God has judged me'. Jacob's blessing calls him a judge of his people and a serpent by the way.
catholic: Jacob interrupts his blessing of Dan with the prayer 'I have waited for your salvation, LORD' (Gen 49:18). Dan is the one tribe missing from the list of the sealed in Rev 7:5-8, which some Fathers connected with Gen 49:17; this is speculation, not Church teaching.
know: Son of Jacob and Bilhah; name means 'he judged' (Gen 30:6)
Father of Hushim (Gen 46:23)
'Dan will judge his people' (Gen 49:16)

name: Darius the Mede
summary: Darius the Mede received Belshazzar's kingdom and set Daniel over his governors. Tricked by jealous officials into signing an irrevocable decree against prayer to anyone but the king, he reluctantly had Daniel thrown to the lions, rejoiced at his deliverance, and decreed reverence for Daniel's God.
know: Called 'son of Ahasuerus, of the offspring of the Medes' (Dan 9:1).
His historical identity is debated.
Distinct from Darius I of Persia in Haggai, Zechariah and Ezra.

name: Dinah
summary: Daughter of Jacob and Leah. When she went out to visit the women of the land, Shechem son of Hamor took and violated her and then sought to marry her; her brothers Simeon and Levi deceived the Shechemites and killed them.
know: Only daughter of Jacob named in Genesis (Gen 30:21)
Violated by Shechem (Gen 34:2)
Avenged by Simeon and Levi (Gen 34:25-26)

name: Ehud
summary: Left-handed Benjamite, son of Gera, raised up by the LORD when Israel had served Eglon king of Moab eighteen years. Bringing tribute, he gained a private audience, killed the obese king with a hidden double-edged sword, escaped, and led Israel to victory; the land had rest eighty years.
catholic: Ehud's 'secret message from God' (Jdg 3:20) has been read allegorically by the Fathers of the two-edged word of God (Heb 4:12) that pierces to the heart. More broadly he shows God choosing the unlikely - a left-handed man of the smallest tribe - to save his people.
know: Left-handed Benjamite (Jdg 3:15).
Killed Eglon of Moab with a hidden sword (Jdg 3:21-22).
Rallied Israel at the fords of the Jordan.
Eighty years of rest followed (Jdg 3:30).

name: Eliphaz (son of Esau)
summary: Firstborn son of Esau by Adah; father of Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam and Kenaz, and of Amalek by his concubine Timna.
know: Father of Amalek (Gen 36:12)
Not the same as Eliphaz the Temanite, Job's friend, though that name echoes his son Teman

name: Elizabeth
summary: Elizabeth, of the priestly line of Aaron and wife of the priest Zechariah, was righteous but barren and advanced in years. She conceived John in her old age, and when her relative Mary visited, the child leapt in her womb and, filled with the Holy Spirit, she greeted Mary as 'the mother of my Lord'. At John's circumcision she insisted he be named John.
catholic: Elizabeth's inspired words 'Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb' form part of the Hail Mary (CCC 2676), and her greeting of Mary as 'the mother of my Lord' is cited by the Church for Mary's divine motherhood (CCC 495). The Visitation (May 31) celebrates her meeting with Mary. Her late, miraculous motherhood echoes Sarah and Hannah and shows that 'nothing is impossible with God' (Lk 1:37).
know: A descendant of Aaron (Lk 1:5).
Relative of the Virgin Mary (Lk 1:36).
First to call Mary 'the mother of my Lord' (Lk 1:43).
Her words are part of the Hail Mary.
feast: September 23 (Sts Zechariah and Elizabeth, Roman Martyrology)

name: Elkanah
summary: Elkanah son of Jeroham, a man of Ramathaim-zophim in the hill country of Ephraim, went up yearly to worship at Shiloh. He had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah, and loved the childless Hannah tenderly. After Samuel's birth he let Hannah fulfil her vow and give the boy to the LORD's service.
catholic: Elkanah is remembered for his gentle love toward his barren wife ('Am I not better to you than ten sons?') and for his faithful yearly pilgrimage, the setting in which Hannah's prayer was heard. The Chronicler lists him among the Levites, so Samuel's priestly ministry has a family background.
know: Lived at Ramah (Ramathaim-zophim) in Ephraim
Husband of Hannah and Peninnah
Father of Samuel and of three more sons and two daughters by Hannah
1 Chronicles 6 counts him among the Kohathite Levites

name: Enosh
summary: Son of Seth and father of Kenan. In his days 'men began to call on the LORD's name'. He lived 905 years.
catholic: The Catechism notes the invocation of the divine name in the time of Enosh as part of the earliest history of prayer (CCC 2569). Luke lists him (as 'Enos') among Jesus' ancestors.
know: In his time people began to call on the LORD's name (Gen 4:26)
Spelled 'Enos' in Luke 3:38
Lived 905 years

name: Felix
summary: Antonius Felix was the Roman governor to whom the tribune Lysias sent Paul under guard. He heard Paul's case against the high priest Ananias and Tertullus but postponed judgment; when Paul spoke of righteousness, self-control and the judgment to come, Felix was terrified, yet he kept Paul in custody for two years hoping for a bribe.
catholic: Felix is a figure of the soul that hears the truth, trembles, and still delays conversion ('when it is a convenient season, I will summon you', Acts 24:25).
know: Governor of Judea at Caesarea.
Husband of Drusilla.
Kept Paul in prison two years hoping for money (Acts 24:26-27).
Succeeded by Porcius Festus.

name: Gabael
summary: The kinsman at Rages in Media with whom Tobit left ten talents of silver; Raphael retrieved the money from him and brought him to Tobias' wedding.
know: Called 'brother of Gabrias' (Tob 1:14) and 'son of Gabrias' (Tob 4:20).
Came to the wedding feast and blessed Tobias (Tob 9:5-6).

name: Gad
summary: Jacob's son by Leah's servant Zilpah; Leah named him saying 'How fortunate!' Jacob foretold that raiders would raid him but he would raid at their heels.
know: Son of Jacob and Zilpah (Gen 30:9-11)
Father of seven sons (Gen 46:16)
Not the prophet Gad of David's time

name: Gilead
summary: Son of Machir and grandson of Manasseh, ancestor of the Gileadite clans including Hepher.
know: Son of Machir (Num 26:29).
Father of Hepher (Num 26:32).

name: Hananiah son of Azzur
summary: Hananiah, a prophet from Gibeon, publicly contradicted Jeremiah in the Temple, prophesying that Babylon's yoke would be broken within two years, and broke the wooden yoke from Jeremiah's neck. Jeremiah answered that God would put an iron yoke on the nations and that Hananiah would die that year; he died two months later.
know: The classic example of a false prophet who tells people what they want to hear (Jer 28).
Broke Jeremiah's wooden yoke; God replaced it with an iron one.
Died in the seventh month of that year, as Jeremiah foretold.

name: Hanun
summary: Hanun son of Nahash humiliated David's envoys of condolence, shaving half their beards, which provoked the Ammonite war in which Uriah later died.
know: Provoked war with David

name: Hoshea
summary: Hoshea son of Elah killed Pekah and became the last king of Israel. A vassal of Shalmaneser of Assyria, he conspired with Egypt and withheld tribute; Shalmaneser imprisoned him and besieged Samaria for three years, and in 722 BC Samaria fell and Israel was deported to Assyria.
catholic: 2 Kings 17 explains the fall of Samaria as the fruit of centuries of idolatry and rejection of the prophets - a sober theological meditation the Church reads as a call to fidelity.
know: Last king of the northern kingdom
Rebelled against Assyria
Samaria fell in his ninth year (722 BC)

name: James, son of Alphaeus
summary: James son of Alphaeus is the ninth name in the lists of the Twelve (Mt 10:3; Mk 3:18; Lk 6:15; Acts 1:13); nothing else is said of him under that name.
catholic: Catholic tradition generally identifies him with 'James the less' (Mk 15:40) and with James 'the brother of the Lord' who led the Jerusalem church, and honours him as St James the Less together with St Philip. The identification is traditional rather than certain.
know: Son of Alphaeus (Mt 10:3).
Traditionally 'St James the Less'.
Catholic tradition generally identifies him with James the brother of the Lord.
Feast May 3, with St Philip.

name: Joash the Abiezrite
summary: Man of Ophrah of the clan of Abiezer in Manasseh, father of Gideon. When the townsmen demanded Gideon's death for destroying Baal's altar, Joash replied, 'If he is a god, let him contend for himself.'
know: Father of Gideon (Jdg 6:11).
Owned the altar of Baal Gideon tore down.
Defended his son (Jdg 6:31).

name: Kenan
summary: Son of Enosh and father of Mahalalel; he lived 910 years.
know: Called 'Cainan' in Luke 3:37
Lived 910 years

name: Mark
summary: John, called Mark, was the son of Mary, in whose Jerusalem house the church gathered. He went with his cousin Barnabas and with Saul on the first missionary journey but turned back at Perga, causing a sharp disagreement that separated Paul and Barnabas. Later reconciled with Paul, he is with him in prison as a fellow worker and is called 'useful to me for service'; Peter calls him 'Mark, my son'.
catholic: The Church honors St Mark as the author of the second Gospel; his feast is April 25 and his symbol is the lion. Early tradition (Papias, via Eusebius) holds that he wrote down Peter's preaching as Peter's interpreter, so that his Gospel transmits the apostolic witness of the head of the apostles. Tradition also holds that he founded the Church of Alexandria and died a martyr there; his relics were brought to Venice, whose patron he is. His restoration to Paul's favor after failure is a picture of reconciliation in the Church.
know: Also called John (Acts 12:12, 13:5, 13:13).
Son of Mary of Jerusalem and cousin of Barnabas (Col 4:10).
Left the first missionary journey at Perga (Acts 13:13; 15:38).
Peter calls him 'my son' (1 Pet 5:13).
Traditionally the evangelist of the second Gospel; feast April 25.

name: Mary of Clopas
summary: Mary 'the wife of Clopas' stood by the cross with the Virgin Mary and Mary Magdalene (Jn 19:25). The Synoptic Gospels name among the women at the cross and tomb 'Mary the mother of James and Joses' (Mt 27:56; Mk 15:40), also called 'the other Mary' (Mt 27:61; 28:1); Catholic tradition generally identifies these as one woman.
catholic: The Catechism points to her to explain the 'brothers of Jesus': 'James and Joses, brothers of Jesus, are the sons of another Mary, a disciple of Christ, whom St Matthew significantly calls the other Mary' (CCC 500). Some readers take John 19:25 to call her the sister (kinswoman) of the Virgin Mary. She is honoured among the holy women who followed Jesus from Galilee and were first at the empty tomb.
know: Wife of Clopas (Jn 19:25).
'Mary the mother of James the less and of Joses' (Mk 15:40) - identification with Mary of Clopas is traditional.
Called 'the other Mary' in Matthew (Mt 28:1).
Brought spices to anoint Jesus' body (Mk 16:1).

name: Matthew (Levi)
summary: Matthew, also called Levi son of Alphaeus, was a tax collector at Capernaum. At Jesus' word 'Follow me' he left his tax booth and hosted a banquet for Jesus with tax collectors and sinners, where Jesus said he came to call not the righteous but sinners.
catholic: The Church honours him as Apostle and Evangelist, by tradition author of the First Gospel, written to show Jesus as the fulfilment of Israel's Scriptures; his symbol is the man (or angel). His call, painted by Caravaggio, is a classic image of grace meeting a sinner. Tradition holds he died a martyr.
know: Called 'Levi the son of Alphaeus' in Mark 2:14.
A tax collector (Mt 9:9; 10:3).
Traditionally author of the Gospel of Matthew.
Feast September 21.

name: Menahem
summary: Menahem son of Gadi killed Shallum, savagely put down resistance at Tiphsah, and reigned ten years, paying Pul (Tiglath-pileser) of Assyria a thousand talents of silver raised from Israel's wealthy men.
know: Paid tribute to Assyria

name: Mushi
summary: Son of Merari and grandson of Levi, listed in the Levitical genealogies; head of a Levite clan.
know: Grandson of Levi through Merari.
Named in the genealogy of Exodus 6 and the census of Numbers 3.

name: Necoh
summary: Pharaoh Necoh (Neco) marched north to aid Assyria; Josiah went out against him at Megiddo and was killed. Necoh then deposed Jehoahaz, made Jehoiakim king and laid tribute on Judah, until Nebuchadnezzar defeated him at Carchemish.
know: Killed Josiah at Megiddo
Deposed Jehoahaz and installed Jehoiakim
Defeated at Carchemish (605 BC)

name: Obed
summary: Son of Boaz and Ruth, born in Bethlehem and nursed by Naomi; the neighbour women named him. He was the father of Jesse and grandfather of King David.
catholic: Matthew and Luke include him in the genealogy of Jesus, so he is one of the links through which the promise to Judah ('the scepter will not depart from Judah', Gen 49:10) passes to David and to Christ.
know: Son of Boaz and Ruth (Ruth 4:13).
Named by the women of Bethlehem (Ruth 4:17).
Father of Jesse, grandfather of David (Ruth 4:17, 22).

name: Peleg
summary: Son of Eber, so named because 'in his days the earth was divided'; father of Reu.
know: Name means 'division' (Gen 10:25)
Listed in Luke 3:35

name: Rahab
summary: Canaanite woman of Jericho, called a prostitute, who hid Joshua's two spies, confessed that 'the LORD your God, he is God in heaven above and on earth beneath', and let them down by a rope from her house on the wall. A scarlet cord in her window marked her household, which was spared when Jericho fell; she lived among Israel and, according to Matthew, married Salmon and became the mother of Boaz.
catholic: Rahab is one of the four women named in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus (Mt 1:5), a sign that the Messiah came for Gentiles and sinners. Hebrews 11:31 praises her faith and James 2:25 her works, so she is a classic witness that faith and works go together. St. Clement of Rome (1 Clement 12) saw in the scarlet cord a sign of redemption through the blood of the Lord, and the Fathers read her house, the only place of safety in the doomed city, as a figure of the Church.
know: Hid the spies and confessed faith in the LORD (Jos 2:9-11).
Scarlet cord in her window (Jos 2:18-21).
Spared with her family at Jericho (Jos 6:22-25).
Mother of Boaz by Salmon (Mt 1:5).
Praised in Heb 11:31 and Jas 2:25.

name: Sheba son of Bichri
summary: Sheba son of Bichri, a Benjaminite, raised a revolt of the northern tribes after Absalom's defeat; a wise woman of Abel Beth Maacah persuaded her city to throw his head over the wall to Joab.
know: Cried 'We have no portion in David'
Killed by the people of Abel

name: Shelah (son of Arpachshad)
summary: Son of Arpachshad and father of Eber.
know: Not the same as Shelah son of Judah
Listed among Jesus' ancestors (Lk 3:35)

name: Shelah (son of Judah)
summary: Judah's third son by Shua's daughter, whom Judah withheld from Tamar for fear he too would die; ancestor of the Shelanite clan.
know: Born at Chezib (Gen 38:5)
Withheld from Tamar (Gen 38:11, 14, 26)
Ancestor of the Shelanites (Num 26:20; 1 Ch 4:21)

name: Uzzah
summary: Uzzah, son of Abinadab, drove the new cart carrying the Ark toward Jerusalem; when the oxen stumbled he put out his hand to steady the Ark and was struck dead.
catholic: Uzzah's death is a classic lesson in reverence for the holy: the Ark was to be carried on poles by Levites, not handled. It sets up David's fear - 'How can the Ark of the LORD come to me?' - which Elizabeth echoes before Mary (Lk 1:43).
know: Touched the Ark and died
David named the place Perez-uzzah
Called Uzza in Chronicles

name: Zimri
summary: Zimri, commander of half the chariots, killed Elah and reigned seven days at Tirzah; when the army made Omri king and besieged the city, Zimri burned the palace over himself.
know: Reigned seven days
Died in the burning palace
'Zimri, murderer of his master' became a taunt (2 Kgs 9:31)

name: Achan
summary: Judahite, son of Carmi, who at the fall of Jericho secretly took a mantle, silver and a wedge of gold that had been devoted to the LORD. Israel was then defeated at Ai; Achan was identified by lot, confessed, and was stoned with his household in the Valley of Achor.
catholic: Achan's hidden sin bringing defeat on all Israel is a scriptural image of the communal dimension of sin, which the Catechism describes: every sin harms the communion of the Church. His confession before Joshua ('give glory to the LORD... and make confession') is often cited in teaching on the confession of sins.
know: Took devoted spoil from Jericho (Jos 7:1, 21).
His sin caused the defeat at Ai.
Identified by lot; confessed (Jos 7:16-21).
Stoned in the Valley of Achor (Jos 7:24-26).
Called Achar, 'the troubler of Israel' (1 Chr 2:7).

name: Elihu son of Barachel
summary: A young Buzite who, angry at Job for justifying himself and at the friends for having no answer, delivered four speeches stressing that God teaches through suffering and is beyond human judgment. He is neither answered by Job nor rebuked by God.
catholic: Elihu's insight that suffering can be a discipline that instructs and saves (Job 33:14-30; 36:15) prepares for the Christian understanding of the medicinal and purifying value of trials.
know: Son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram (Job 32:2).
Speaks in Job 32-37.

name: Goliath
summary: Goliath of Gath, a giant Philistine champion, defied the armies of Israel for forty days until the shepherd boy David, trusting in the LORD, felled him with a stone from his sling and cut off his head with the giant's own sword.
catholic: The Fathers read David's victory over Goliath as a figure of Christ's victory over Satan: the humble shepherd from Bethlehem defeats the proud enemy with the weakest means, 'that all the earth may know there is a God in Israel'. Augustine and Caesarius of Arles preached on this typology.
know: About six cubits and a span tall
Defied Israel for forty days
Killed by David's sling stone
His sword was later kept at Nob

name: Habakkuk
summary: Habakkuk prophesied as Babylon rose to power (late 7th century BC), boldly asking God why he tolerates injustice and why he would use the ruthless Chaldeans. God answers that the vision will come in its time and that 'the righteous will live by his faith'; the book ends with a psalm of trust. In the Greek story of Bel and the Dragon, an angel carries 'the prophet Habakkuk' to Babylon to bring food to Daniel in the lions' den.
catholic: Hab 2:4, 'the righteous will live by his faith', is quoted three times in the New Testament (Rom 1:17; Gal 3:11; Heb 10:38) and is central to the Church's teaching on faith as the beginning of salvation. His canticle (Hab 3) is used at Morning Prayer in the Liturgy of the Hours, and his final confession, 'though the fig tree does not flourish... yet I will rejoice in the LORD' (Hab 3:17-18), is a classic of hope in desolation.
know: Dialogues with God about evil (Hab 1-2).
'The righteous will live by his faith' (Hab 2:4).
Carried by an angel to feed Daniel in the lions' den (Dan 14:33-39).

name: Joseph of Arimathea
summary: Joseph of Arimathea was a rich and respected member of the council, a good and righteous man looking for the Kingdom of God, who had not consented to the council's decision. A secret disciple, he boldly asked Pilate for Jesus' body, wrapped it in clean linen and laid it in his own new tomb cut in the rock.
catholic: Joseph fulfils the prophecy that the Servant would be 'with a rich man in his death' (Is 53:9) and is cited with Nicodemus as a secret disciple among the leaders (CCC 595). His care for Jesus' body is honoured in the Fourteenth Station of the Cross and in the corporal work of mercy of burying the dead. Medieval legends link him with Glastonbury and the Holy Grail, but these are not historical tradition.
know: A rich council member from Arimathaea (Mt 27:57; Lk 23:50-51).
Asked Pilate for Jesus' body (Mk 15:43).
Laid Jesus in his own new tomb (Mt 27:60).
Commemorated with Nicodemus on August 31.
feast: August 31 (Sts Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus, Roman Martyrology)

name: Lamech (father of Noah)
summary: Son of Methuselah in the line of Seth. At Noah's birth he prophesied that the child would bring comfort from the toil caused by the cursed ground. He lived 777 years.
catholic: His hope that Noah would bring 'comfort' (Gen 5:29) expresses the longing for relief from the curse that runs through the primeval story. Luke lists him among Jesus' ancestors (Lk 3:36).
know: Father of Noah (Gen 5:28-29)
Named Noah hoping he would bring comfort
Lived 777 years
Different from Lamech son of Methushael
